title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 43
paragraphs: These things tended toward peace for the Ionians. But at the beginning of spring, when the other commanders had all been removed by the king, Mardonius son of Gobryas came down to the coast, bringing with him a very large land-army and a very large naval force. He was a young man, and had lately married Artozostra daughter of King Darius. When Mardonius, leading this army, came to Cilicia, he himself embarked on a ship and proceeded with the other ships, while other leaders led the land-army to the Hellespont. Mardonius, sailing along the coast of Asia, came to Ionia; and here I shall relate something that will be a great marvel to those Hellenes who do not believe that Otanes declared, among the seven men of the Persians, that the Persians ought to have popular rule. For Mardonius deposed all the tyrants of the Ionians and established popular governments in the cities. Having done so, he hurried on to the Hellespont; and when a vast number of ships and a large land-army had been gathered, they crossed the Hellespont in the ships and began to make their way through Europe—and their way was directed against Eretria and Athens.
